meta.notice: Demo route catalogue. Entry requirements, costs and institution names are illustrative and NOT verified against current official sources. `dataAsOf` drives the staleness warning shown in the UI.

routes.name: Science–Maths track towards engineering
routes.summary: A general upper-secondary science track aimed at engineering or applied-science faculties.
strengths: Keeps the widest range of university options open
Strong demand in engineering and applied technology
limitations: Long time before earning; typically four more years after ม.6
Heavy maths and physics load that is difficult to switch out of late
routes.nextExperiment: Spend one weekend following an engineering teardown video and rebuilding the explanation in your own words. Notice whether the detail energises or drains you.

routes.name: Vocational ปวช. — Digital and IT
routes.summary: One of the 12 ปวช. 2567 subject areas, mixing classroom study with practical digital work.
strengths: Lower cost and usually available closer to home
Practical portfolio work from the first year
Can continue to ปวส. or a technology bachelor's degree later
limitations: Some university programmes still prefer the general track
routes.nextExperiment: Build one tiny thing end to end this week — a one-page site, a small automation, a repaired device — and write down which part you enjoyed.

routes.name: Dual vocational education (ทวิภาคี)
routes.summary: Study combined with paid placement at a partner employer, alternating college and workplace.
strengths: Earning and learning at the same time
Real workplace experience before you finish
limitations: Places depend on which employers partner with your college
Narrower specialisation, harder to change direction later
routes.nextExperiment: Find one company near you that takes ทวิภาคี students and ask what a first-year placement actually involves.

routes.name: Arts track towards design and creative work
routes.summary: An arts-leaning track towards communication design, architecture or digital media.
strengths: Portfolio counts as much as exam scores in many programmes
Skills transfer across media, product and marketing work
limitations: Entry is portfolio-driven, which takes sustained work to build
routes.nextExperiment: Redesign one thing you use weekly — a form, a poster, an app screen — and show it to two people who use it.

routes.name: Business and administration
routes.summary: Accounting, marketing or business administration, available through both general and vocational tracks.
strengths: Available at both vocational colleges and universities
Skills apply across almost every industry
limitations: Very common qualification, so experience matters more than the certificate
Wide field — you still have to choose a specialism later
routes.nextExperiment: Run the money or scheduling side of one small real thing — a club event, a family shop's stock list — for two weeks.

routes.name: Health and care pathway
routes.summary: Nursing, allied health or care work, through either the science track or a vocational health programme.
strengths: Consistent demand and a clear professional ladder
limitations: Entry requirements are strict and specific — verify each programme
Emotionally demanding; shift work is normal
routes.nextExperiment: Shadow or interview someone doing the day-to-day version of the job, not the version shown on television.

weeks.objective: Test whether the analytical part actually holds your attention
tasks: Pick one topic from the route and study it for 45 minutes, three times
Write half a page explaining it to someone two years younger
Note honestly when you got bored

weeks.objective: Find out what the work looks like in practice
tasks: Find two people doing this job and read or watch them describe a normal day
List three things you did not expect
Write one question you still cannot answer
Look up the actual current requirements from an official source
Write down the gap between where you are and what is required
Identify the one subject that matters most

weeks.objective: Decide what would change your mind
tasks: Write the strongest argument against this route for you specifically
Talk it through with a counsellor or an adult who knows you
Decide whether to keep, park, or drop this route
Choose the smallest useful project in this direction
Finish it, even badly, within the week
Write down which part you would happily repeat
Find one local college or employer offering this route
Ask what a first-year student actually does day to day
Note the difference from what you imagined

weeks.objective: Test the routine, not the highlight
tasks: Do the least glamorous part of the work for two sessions
Rate your energy after each one
Decide whether the routine is tolerable
Show what you made to someone who does this work
Ask what they would do differently
Decide whether to keep, park, or drop this route

weeks.objective: Start a portfolio piece, not a plan
tasks: Pick one thing that annoys you and redesign it
Keep every rough draft, not just the final
Write two sentences on what you were trying to fix

weeks.objective: Put it in front of real people
tasks: Show it to two people who would actually use it
Write down what confused them
Revise once based on what they said
Find two programmes and read what their portfolio actually requires
List what you are missing
Pick the next piece to make
Read about early-career reality in this field, including income
Talk to a counsellor about the risk
Decide whether to keep, park, or drop this route
Take charge of the money, schedule, or records for one real activity
Keep it accurate for the whole week
Note where you slipped and why
Interview one person working in this area
Ask what the boring 80% of the job is
Write down whether that 80% sounds bearable
Find the current entry requirements from an official source
Write down the realistic total cost
Identify who could help you cover it
List what would make you confident, and what would put you off
Discuss with a counsellor
Decide whether to keep, park, or drop this route
